PyTorch stores GRU gates in reset/update/new order `(r,z,n)`. Its candidate is `n=tanh(W_in*x+b_in+r*(W_hn*h+b_hn))`, and `h_new=(1-z)*n+z*h`; reset multiplies the recurrent affine result, including its bias. Suggested reference: copy each GRU layer’s `weight_ih_l{k}`, `weight_hh_l{k}`, and both biases into a corresponding `GRUCell`. Disable dropout, preserve initial states, and process layers bottom-up at each timestep, feeding each layer’s current output into the next. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html)

For left-padded histories, implement `h=where(valid_t,cell(x_t,h),h)` at every layer; zero input alone does not suppress recurrent updates. For the packed comparison, move valid tokens into chronological prefixes before packing; passing lengths with the original left-padded tensor packs the wrong positions. Compare aligned valid outputs and every layer’s final hidden state. Read the final nonpadding position—`L-1` for nonempty, strictly left-padded histories—never `count-1` in original coordinates. Handle empty histories separately. These checks follow from packing’s prefix-length semantics. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html)

Recommended validation: independent float64 CPU copies, identical inputs/weights, and the same scalar loss over aligned valid outputs/final states. Compare outputs plus input, initial-state, and every parameter gradient with explicit absolute/relative tolerances; padded-input gradients should vanish. Then test CUDA float32 separately, comparing each history alone, in different batch sizes, and with different companion lengths. PyTorch documents that batched versus sliced computations can differ numerically; CUDA kernels and reduction ordering can therefore produce shape-dependent discrepancies. Repeating one identical execution tests repeatability, not batch-shape sensitivity. Float64 agreement supports semantic correctness but does not guarantee bitwise CUDA equality. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)
